sanskrit: yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo 'mbuvegāḥ; samudram evābhimukhā dravanti tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā; viśanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti
english: As the many torrents of the rivers race straight toward the sea, so do these heroes of the world of men enter your blazing mouths.

sanskrit: yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṃgā; viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokās; tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ
english: As moths in headlong speed plunge into a blazing fire to their destruction, so too do these peoples plunge into your mouths in headlong speed, to their destruction.

sanskrit: lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl; lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṃ; bhāsas tavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo
english: Devouring on every side, you lick up all the worlds with your flaming mouths; filling the whole universe with radiance, your terrible splendors scorch it, O Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugrarūpo; namo 'stu te devavara prasīda vijñātum icchāmi bhavantam ādyaṃ; na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim
english: Tell me who you are, you of terrible form. Homage to you, O best of gods; be gracious. I long to know you, the Primal One, for I do not comprehend your working.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca kālo 'smi lokakṣayakṛt pravṛddho; lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ ṛte 'pi tvā na bhaviṣyanti sarve; ye 'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time, grown mighty, the destroyer of the worlds, set in motion here to annihilate the worlds. Even without you, all these warriors arrayed in the opposing ranks shall cease to be.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva; jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva; nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin
english: Therefore rise up and win glory; conquer your foes and enjoy a flourishing kingdom. By me alone are these already slain; be you merely the instrument, O Savyasācin.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca; karṇaṃ tathānyān api yodhavīrān mayā hatāṃs tvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā; yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān
english: Droṇa and Bhīṣma and Jayadratha, and Karṇa, and the other warrior-heroes as well — slay them, already slain by me. Do not falter. Fight! You shall conquer your rivals in battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac chrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya; kṛtāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ; sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing this speech of Keśava, the Diademed One, trembling, his palms joined, made obeisance, and bowing low spoke once more to Kṛṣṇa in a faltering voice, sore afraid.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā; jagat prahṛṣyaty anurajyate ca rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti; sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṃghāḥ
english: Arjuna said: Rightly, O Hṛṣīkeśa, does the world rejoice and take delight in your glory; the rākṣasas flee in terror to every quarter, and all the hosts of the siddhas bow before you.

sanskrit: kasmāc ca te na nameran mahātman; garīyase brahmaṇo 'py ādikartre ananta deveśa jagannivāsa; tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat tatparaṃ yat
english: And why should they not bow to you, O great-souled one, greater even than Brahmā, the first creator? O infinite Lord of gods, abode of the universe, you are the Imperishable, the existent, the non-existent, and what lies beyond both.

sanskrit: tvam ādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇas; tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma; tvayā tataṃ viśvam anantarūpa
english: You are the primal God, the ancient Spirit; you are the supreme resting-place of this universe. You are the knower and the known, the highest abode; by you the universe is pervaded, O you of infinite form.

sanskrit: vāyur yamo 'gnir varuṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ; prajāpatis tvaṃ prapitāmahaś ca namo namas te 'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ; punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te
english: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon, Prajāpati, and the great-grandsire. Homage, homage to you a thousandfold, and again and yet again, homage, homage to you!

sanskrit: namaḥ purastād atha pṛṣṭhatas te; namo 'stu te sarvata eva sarva anantavīryāmitavikramas tvaṃ; sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ
english: Homage to you from before and from behind; homage to you on every side, O All. Of infinite valor and boundless might, you encompass all things, and therefore you are all.

sanskrit: sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yad uktaṃ; he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedaṃ; mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi
english: Whatever I said rashly, thinking you but a friend — 'Hey Kṛṣṇa! Hey Yādava! Hey friend!' — in ignorance of this your majesty, through heedlessness or through affection,

sanskrit: yac cāvahāsārtham asatkṛto 'si; vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu eko 'tha vāpy acyuta tatsamakṣaṃ; tat kṣāmaye tvām aham aprameyam
english: and however, for jest's sake, I slighted you at play, in bed, while seated, or at meals, whether alone or before others, O Acyuta — for that I beg your pardon, O immeasurable one.

sanskrit: pitāsi lokasya carācarasya; tvam asya pūjyaś ca gurur garīyān na tvatsamo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyo; lokatraye 'py apratimaprabhāva
english: You are the father of the world, of all that moves and is still; you are its object of worship, its venerable teacher. There is none equal to you — how then could there be another greater? — in the three worlds, O you of incomparable power.

sanskrit: tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ; prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ; priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum
english: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I implore your grace, O Lord, worthy of praise. As a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with his beloved, so should you bear with me, O God.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito 'smi dṛṣṭvā; bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me tad eva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ; prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
english: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me, O God, that other form of yours; be gracious, O Lord of gods, abode of the universe.

sanskrit: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahastam; icchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭum ahaṃ tathaiva tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena; sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte
english: I long to see you just as before, crowned with the diadem, bearing the mace and the discus in your hand. Take on once more that four-armed form, O thousand-armed one, O you whose body is the universe.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ; rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitam ātmayogāt tejomayaṃ viśvam anantam ādyaṃ; yan me tvad anyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam
english: The Blessed Lord said: By my grace, O Arjuna, and through my own power, this supreme form of mine has been shown to you — full of light, universal, infinite, primal — which none but you has ever beheld.

sanskrit: na vedayajñādhyayanair na dānair; na ca kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ evaṃrūpaḥ śakya ahaṃ nṛloke; draṣṭuṃ tvad anyena kurupravīra
english: Not by study of the Vedas and sacrifices, not by gifts, not by rites, not by fierce austerities, can I be seen in this form in the world of men by any other than you, O foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo; dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoram īdṛṅ mamedam vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punas tvaṃ; tad eva me rūpam idaṃ prapaśya
english: Let there be no fear in you, no bewilderment, at beholding this dread form of mine. Free from fear, glad of heart, behold once more this very form of mine.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity arjunaṃ vāsudevas tathoktvā; svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayām āsa bhūyaḥ āśvāsayām āsa ca bhītam enaṃ; bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapur mahātmā
english: Saṃjaya said: Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Vāsudeva revealed again his own form, and the great-souled one, becoming once more gentle of aspect, comforted him in his terror.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana idānīm asmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ
english: Arjuna said: Beholding this gentle human form of yours, O Janārdana, I am now composed, my mind restored, returned to my natural state.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca sudurdarśam idaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to behold; even the gods forever long for the sight of this form.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ vedair na tapasā na dānena na cejyayā śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi māṃ yathā
english: Not by the Vedas, not by austerity, not by almsgiving, nor by sacrifice, can I be seen in such a form as you have seen me.

sanskrit: bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṃvidho 'rjuna jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca paraṃtapa
english: But by undivided devotion, O Arjuna, can I in this form be known and truly seen and entered into, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: matkarmakṛn matparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava
english: He who does my work, who holds me supreme, who is devoted to me, freed from attachment, without enmity toward any being — he comes to me, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktās tvāṃ paryupāsate ye cāpy akṣaram avyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ
english: Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship you, and those who worship the Imperishable, the Unmanifest — which of these are the better versed in yoga?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca mayy āveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: Those who fix their minds on me and, ever steadfast, worship me, endowed with supreme faith — these I deem the most perfect in yoga.

sanskrit: ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṃ paryupāsate sarvatragam acintyaṃ ca kūṭastham acalaṃ dhruvam
english: But those who worship the Imperishable, the indefinable, the Unmanifest, the all-pervading and unthinkable, the changeless, the immovable, the eternal,

sanskrit: saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
english: restraining the whole host of the senses, even-minded toward all, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings — they too attain me.

sanskrit: kleśo 'dhikataras teṣām avyaktāsaktacetasām avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṃ dehavadbhir avāpyate
english: Greater is the toil of those whose minds are fixed upon the Unmanifest; for the goal of the Unmanifest is hard for the embodied to reach.

sanskrit: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate
english: But those who, renouncing all their actions in me and holding me supreme, worship me, meditating on me with undivided yoga —

sanskrit: teṣām ahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt bhavāmi nacirāt pārtha mayy āveśitacetasām
english: of these, whose thought is set on me, I become ere long the deliverer from the ocean of death-bound transmigration, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya nivasiṣyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding rest in me; thereafter you shall dwell in me alone — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram abhyāsayogena tato mām icchāptuṃ dhanaṃjaya
english: But if you cannot fix your thought steadily upon me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of repeated practice, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: abhyāse 'py asamartho 'si matkarmaparamo bhava madartham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi
english: If you are unable even in practice, be intent on works done for my sake; doing your deeds for my sake, you shall attain perfection.

sanskrit: athaitad apy aśakto 'si kartuṃ madyogam āśritaḥ sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān
english: And if you are unable to do even this, then, taking refuge in union with me, renounce the fruit of all action, with the self subdued.

sanskrit: śreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṃ viśiṣyate dhyānāt karmaphalatyāgas tyāgāc chāntir anantaram
english: For knowledge is better than practice, and meditation surpasses knowledge, and the renunciation of the fruit of action is better than meditation; from renunciation peace follows at once.

sanskrit: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī
english: He who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from the sense of 'mine' and from egoism, the same in pain and pleasure, forbearing,

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ mayy arpitamanobuddhir yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
english: ever content, the yogin, self-controlled, of firm resolve, his mind and understanding offered up to me — such a devotee of mine is dear to me.

sanskrit: yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate ca yaḥ harṣāmarṣabhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ
english: He from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world, who is freed from elation, impatience, fear, and agitation — he too is dear to me.

sanskrit: anapekṣaḥ śucir dakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
english: Free from expectation, pure, capable, indifferent, untroubled, renouncing every undertaking — such a devotee of mine is dear to me.

sanskrit: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ
english: He who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, who has renounced both the fair and the foul, and is full of devotion — he is dear to me.

sanskrit: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāvamānayoḥ śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ
english: The same to foe and to friend, the same in honor and dishonor, the same in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, freed from attachment,

sanskrit: tulyanindāstutir maunī saṃtuṣṭo yena kena cit aniketaḥ sthiramatir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ
english: alike in blame and praise, silent, content with whatever comes, with no fixed abode, steadfast in mind, full of devotion — that man is dear to me.

sanskrit: ye tu dharmyāmṛtam idaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktās te 'tīva me priyāḥ
english: But those who honor this nectar of dharma as it has been declared, full of faith, holding me supreme — those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetram ity abhidhīyate etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ
english: The Blessed Lord said: This body, O son of Kuntī, is called the field; and him who knows it, those who know such things call the knower of the field.

sanskrit: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata kṣetrakṣetrajñayor jñānaṃ yat taj jñānaṃ mataṃ mama
english: Know me too as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata. The knowledge of the field and its knower — that I hold to be true knowledge.

sanskrit: tat kṣetraṃ yac ca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataś ca yat sa ca yo yatprabhāvaś ca tat samāsena me śṛṇu
english: What that field is, and of what nature, and with what modifications, and whence it arises; and who he is, and what his powers — hear this from me in brief.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṃ chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak brahmasūtrapadaiś caiva hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ
english: It has been sung in many ways by the seers, severally in the diverse Vedic hymns, and also in the words of the aphorisms on Brahman, reasoned and well-determined.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāny ahaṃkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ca indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ
english: The great elements, egoism, the intellect, and the Unmanifest; the eleven senses, and the five objects of the senses;

sanskrit: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃghātaś cetanā dhṛtiḥ etat kṣetraṃ samāsena savikāram udāhṛtam
english: desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, consciousness, steadfastness — this, in brief, is the field declared together with its modifications.

sanskrit: amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṃsā kṣāntir ārjavam ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyam ātmavinigrahaḥ
english: Humility, freedom from pretense, non-violence, forbearance, uprightness, service to one's teacher, purity, steadiness, self-restraint;

sanskrit: indriyārtheṣu vairāgyam anahaṃkāra eva ca janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam
english: dispassion toward the objects of sense, and absence of egoism; insight into the evil of birth, death, old age, sickness, and pain;

sanskrit: asaktir anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu nityaṃ ca samacittatvam iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu
english: non-attachment, freedom from clinging to son, wife, home, and the rest; and constant evenness of mind amid the befalling of the desired and the undesired;

sanskrit: mayi cānanyayogena bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī viviktadeśasevitvam aratir janasaṃsadi
english: unswerving devotion to me through undivided yoga, resort to solitary places, and distaste for the throng of people;

sanskrit: adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṃ yad ato 'nyathā
english: constancy in the knowledge of the Self, and insight into the goal of the knowledge of truth — this is declared to be knowledge; and ignorance is whatever differs from this.

sanskrit: jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute anādimat paraṃ brahma na sat tan nāsad ucyate
english: I shall now declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the supreme Brahman, without beginning, of which it is said neither that it is existent nor non-existent.

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādaṃ tat sarvatokṣiśiromukham sarvataḥśrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, with ears on every side, it stands enveloping all things in the world.

sanskrit: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam asaktaṃ sarvabhṛc caiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca
english: Shining through the functions of all the senses, yet devoid of all the senses; unattached, yet the support of all; free from the strands of nature, yet their enjoyer.

sanskrit: bahir antaś ca bhūtānām acaraṃ caram eva ca sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat
english: Without and within all beings, unmoving yet moving; by reason of its subtlety it is unknowable, and it is far off and yet near.

sanskrit: avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam bhūtabhartṛ ca taj jñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
english: Undivided, yet abiding as though divided among beings; that which is to be known is the sustainer of beings, their devourer, and their creator.

sanskrit: jyotiṣām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param ucyate jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
english: It is the light even of lights, said to be beyond all darkness; it is knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the goal of knowledge, seated in the heart of all.

sanskrit: iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ madbhakta etad vijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate
english: Thus the field, and likewise knowledge, and that which is to be known, have been told in brief. My devotee, understanding this, attains to my being.

sanskrit: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś caiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān
english: Know that both Nature and the Spirit are without beginning; and know that the modifications and the strands of nature arise from Nature.

sanskrit: kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate
english: In the production of effect and cause and agency, Nature is said to be the cause; the Spirit is said to be the cause in the experiencing of pleasures and pains.

sanskrit: puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijān guṇān kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo 'sya sadasadyonijanmasu
english: For the Spirit, seated in Nature, experiences the strands born of Nature; attachment to the strands is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.

sanskrit: upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ paramātmeti cāpy ukto dehe 'smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ
english: The witness, the consenter, the sustainer, the enjoyer, the Great Lord, and also called the Supreme Self — such is the supreme Spirit within this body.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha sarvathā vartamāno 'pi na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate
english: He who thus knows the Spirit and Nature together with its strands, in whatever state he may live, is not born again.

sanskrit: dhyānenātmani paśyanti ke cid ātmānam ātmanā anye sāṃkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare
english: By meditation some behold the Self in the self by the self; others by the yoga of knowledge, and yet others by the yoga of action.

sanskrit: anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate te 'pi cātitaranty eva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ
english: But others, not knowing thus, worship having heard it from others; they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.

sanskrit: yāvat saṃjāyate kiṃ cit sattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
english: Whatever being comes into existence, whether unmoving or moving, know that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram vinaśyatsv avinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
english: He who sees the Supreme Lord abiding alike in all beings, the imperishable amid the perishing — he truly sees.

sanskrit: samaṃ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram na hinasty ātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim
english: For seeing the Lord present alike everywhere, he does not destroy the Self by the self, and thereby he attains the supreme goal.

sanskrit: prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ yaḥ paśyati tathātmānam akartāraṃ sa paśyati
english: He who sees that actions are in every way performed by Nature alone, and the Self as the non-doer — he truly sees.

sanskrit: yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvam ekastham anupaśyati tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When he perceives the separate existence of beings as resting in the One, and their expansion from that alone, then he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: anāditvān nirguṇatvāt paramātmāyam avyayaḥ śarīrastho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
english: Being beginningless and free from the strands of nature, this imperishable Supreme Self, though dwelling in the body, O son of Kuntī, neither acts nor is tainted.

sanskrit: yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyād ākāśaṃ nopalipyate sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate
english: As the all-pervading ether, by reason of its subtlety, is never tainted, so the Self, abiding everywhere in the body, is never tainted.
